Issues.Title: Correct BPE pre-tokenization whitespace documentation
Issues.Body:
Adjusts the documentation added in #7716 by moving the whitespace guidance from `BpeOptions.ByteLevel` to `BpeOptions.PreTokenizer`.

Whitespace removal is not related to the `ByteLevel` setting. When no pre-tokenizer is specified, BPE uses `PreTokenizer.CreateWordOrNonWord()`, which discards whitespace with either value of `ByteLevel`. Byte-level mapping operates on the retained segments; it does not configure pre-tokenization or preserve characters excluded by the pre-tokenizer.

The remark also clarifies that each segment is encoded independently, so BPE merges cannot cross segment boundaries. To preserve whitespace during pre-tokenization, callers should select rules matching the model, such as the GPT-2 pattern where appropriate. No exception or runtime behavior change is needed.

Documentation-only change.

Closes #7715

/cc @lunosia
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "Correct BPE pre-tokenization whitespace documentation" (#7789)

Issues.Title: Add missing XML documentation to public APIs
Issues.Body:
## Goal

Add missing XML documentation to public APIs, including publicly accessible protected members, so that IntelliSense and generated API reference documentation cover the API surface.

## Basic inventory

A diagnostic build at commit 272f2fb0abc7ef841597da0e680992d4bfdc37fc found **6,459 distinct types/members missing XML documentation in 34 projects**, plus **238 additional undocumented members suppressed by source-level pragmas**.

### Stable-version projects (1.x and later)

| Project | Missing XML documentation |
|---|---:|
| Microsoft.ML.Data | 108 |
| Microsoft.ML.Transforms | 73 |
| Microsoft.ML.TimeSeries | 44 |
| Microsoft.ML.Core | 41 |
| Microsoft.ML.StandardTrainers | 34 |
| Microsoft.ML.DataView | 32 |
| Microsoft.ML.LightGbm | 29 |
| Microsoft.ML.ImageAnalytics | 28 |
| Microsoft.ML.FastTree | 18 |
| Microsoft.ML.OnnxTransformer | 17 |
| Microsoft.ML.Vision | 13 |
| Microsoft.ML.KMeansClustering | 5 |
| Microsoft.ML.Mkl.Components | 5 |
| Microsoft.ML.PCA | 5 |
| Microsoft.ML.TensorFlow | 3 |
| Microsoft.Extensions.ML | 2 |
| Microsoft.ML.Tokenizers | 1 |
| **Total** | **458** |

### Pre-1.0 projects (0.x)

| Project | Missing XML documentation |
|---|---:|
| Microsoft.Data.Analysis | 5,153 |
| Microsoft.ML.AutoML | 371 |
| Microsoft.ML.Sweeper | 228 |
| Microsoft.ML.TorchSharp | 110 |
| Microsoft.ML.Fairlearn | 40 |
| Microsoft.ML.ResultProcessor | 31 |
| Microsoft.ML.SamplesUtils | 28 |
| Microsoft.ML.AutoML.Interactive | 16 |
| Microsoft.Data.Analysis.Interactive | 5 |
| Microsoft.ML.CodeGenerator | 5 |
| Microsoft.ML.Maml | 4 |
| Microsoft.ML.Console | 2 |
| Microsoft.ML.DnnAnalyzer | 2 |
| Microsoft.ML.Experimental | 2 |
| Microsoft.ML.Recommender | 2 |
| Microsoft.ML.OneDal | 1 |
| Microsoft.ML.OnnxConverter | 1 |
| **Total** | **6,001** |

## Main concentrations and examples

- **Data.Analysis:** 4,898 of its 5,153 gaps are in two T4-generated files: `PrimitiveDataFrameColumn.BinaryOperationAPIs.ExplodedColumns.cs` (3,151) and `PrimitiveDataFrameColumn.BinaryOperators.cs` (1,747). Update the corresponding `.tt` templates and regenerate their outputs rather than hand-editing generated files.
- **Source-level suppression:** another 238 distinct Data.Analysis members are missing documentation in `DataFrame.BinaryOperators.cs` and `DataFrameColumn.BinaryOperators.cs`, where `#pragma warning disable 1591` remains active. These are not included in the tables.
- **AutoML:** 227 of its 371 gaps are in source-generator output; these should be addressed in the generator.
- **Ordinary API gaps:** examples include `AutoMLExperiment`'s constructor and `SetTrainingTimeInSeconds`, `DataViewRowId.CompareTo` and `Equals(DataViewRowId)`, and the span-based `BertTokenizer.CreateTokenTypeIdsFromSequences` overload. The last example is the only gap found in Tokenizers.

## Incremental enforcement

**CS1591 could be enabled in an individual project once all of its APIs are documented**, without waiting for the entire repository to be clean.

For each completed project, remove its effective CS1591 suppression, including the suppression inherited from `src/Directory.Build.props` and any project-specific or source-level suppressions. Once clean, also remove CS1591 from its effective `WarningsNotAsErrors` so that the existing warnings-as-errors policy prevents new documentation gaps. This should be done selectively for completed projects while unfinished projects retain their suppressions.

Issues.Title: Add labels to DataFrameColumn.Info output
Issues.Body:
Fixes #6274

`DataFrameColumn.Info()` currently returns the data type and non-null count without labels. Add the resource labels used by `DataFrame.Info()` so these values are understandable when inspecting a single column.

For example, an integer column with three non-null values now returns:

```text
DataType: System.Int32
Length (excluding null values): 3
```

The public virtual signature and two-row structure are unchanged. The returned strings intentionally include labels, so callers parsing the previous strings may need updating.

`DataFrame.Info()` keeps its existing table output by removing matching label prefixes from each column's virtual `Info()` result. It clones the result before modification to avoid mutating cached values returned by overrides.

Regression tests cover numeric, string, and Arrow string columns; empty and null-containing columns; the existing table output; and custom overrides with cached results.

## Validation

- Microsoft.Data.Analysis build: passed for netstandard2.0 and net8.0, with zero warnings and errors.
- Official Microsoft.Data.Analysis.Tests project, net8.0, filter `FullyQualifiedName~Info`: 16 passed, including all 9 Info cases.
- Changed-file whitespace verification and `git diff --check`: passed.

The build used the repository-pinned SDK and `/p:SkipRuntimesInstall=true` with an installed .NET 8 runtime. Full-repository CI and other test target frameworks have not been run locally.

## Checklist

- [x] Descriptive title.
- [x] Associated issue referenced.
- [x] Description explains the change, approach, and behavior implications.
- [x] Necessary tests included in this PR.

Issues.Title: Enable Unix Helix crash dump capture
Issues.Body:
## Summary
Enable .NET dumps, JSON crash reports, and dump-generation diagnostic logging in the Unix Helix runner when HELIX_DUMP_FOLDER is set. Document where to find the artifacts.

## Motivation
While validating #7747, [build 1629902](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1629902) failed with an unrelated crash: the main `Microsoft.ML.Tests` process exited with SIGSEGV (139) on macOS x64 Debug. The main test process crashed while tests were still running, rather than during shutdown.

The console log ended just after an image-creation test started, but several tests were running concurrently. Helix uploaded no dump or crash report, despite the shell printing "core dumped", so there was no crashing-thread stack or process state to identify the faulting code. The available evidence was insufficient to determine the cause or establish whether the crash was related to the PR.

Enabling capture preserves evidence from future crashes instead of relying on the last test logged or waiting for a local reproduction. The JSON report provides thread stacks that can be inspected without a matching-OS debugger; the dump allows deeper analysis of memory, modules, and thread state with the matching runtime and native binaries. Writing them to Helix's dump directory makes them available as work-item artifacts, and diagnostic logging helps explain any capture failure.

## Actual CI validation
[Build 1632277](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1632277) ran a temporary fatal native-memory-access probe on macOS x64 in both Debug and Release. Both processes exited with SIGSEGV (139), and both Helix work items uploaded a dump and readable JSON crash report. The reports identify the crashing thread and include DumpCaptureProbeTests.CaptureSegmentationFault plus native frames.

- [Debug crash report](https://helixr1107v0xdeko0k025g8.blob.core.windows.net/dotnet-machinelearning-refs-pull-7780-merge-2b02312c4c2a4317bf/Microsoft.ML.Tests/1/coredump.68046.1791823117.dmp.crashreport.json?helixlogtype=result)
- [Release crash report](https://helixr1107v0xdeko0k025g8.blob.core.windows.net/dotnet-machinelearning-refs-pull-7780-merge-efff89a63ce5409f86/Microsoft.ML.Tests/1/coredump.15665.1791822990.dmp.crashreport.json?helixlogtype=result)

The probe and temporary test filtering were removed in a follow-up commit. The final diff contains only the runner configuration and documentation.

Issues.Title: Remove TensorFlow
Issues.Body:
Remove TensorFlow from ML.NET while retaining `Microsoft.ML.Vision` and its existing image-classification workflow. The goal is minimal user disruption and implementation cost. This should be an internal backend replacement, not a package reorganisation, a new training API, or a requirement for users to rewrite their pipelines.

## Proposed approach

Keep the Vision package, catalogue entry points, trainer/model types and ordinary application call sites.

The current image classifier uses a frozen pretrained network to extract features, then trains a single dense classification layer using mini-batch gradient descent. The proposed replacement is:

- ONNX Runtime for the existing pretrained feature-extraction networks.
- A narrow managed implementation of the existing classification head, reusing suitable ML.NET numerical primitives.
- The existing Vision orchestration for batching, learning-rate scheduling, validation, early stopping, callbacks and feature caching.

This is not a switch to a different ML.NET classifier. Existing training options must retain meaningful behaviour.

### Feasibility gate

Before committing to this implementation, prove that the existing pretrained models can be converted and used without unacceptable behavioural or performance changes.

Start with the default `ResnetV250` architecture:

- Inspect its original model assets and weight dependencies, then convert the actual input-to-bottleneck graph to ONNX.
- Verify preprocessing and feature outputs against the original implementation on a fixed image set.
- Verify classification-head updates, loss calculation, label mapping and partial batches independently.
- Preserve the existing flower-classification quality thresholds.
- Establish redistribution rights, checksums and a reliable distribution route for the converted assets.

Then establish equivalent support for the remaining architectures.

Do not silently substitute different networks, such as replacing ResNet V2 with an existing ONNX ResNet V1 model. If an architecture cannot be preserved at reasonable cost, make that an explicit decision before proceeding.

## Remove TensorFlow dependencies

Remove the TensorFlow integration, graph-specific APIs, internal TensorFlow retraining implementation and TensorFlow-only DnnAnalyzer utility.

Update the affected project references, solution entries, central package definitions, build metadata, generated-project templates, samples and documentation. Remove `TensorFlow.NET`, `SciSharp.TensorFlow.Redist*` and TensorFlow-only test-model dependencies.

Preserve Vision scenarios before deleting the TensorFlow test project. Keep shared image datasets, ONNX infrastructure and unrelated tests.

Existing ONNX functionality, public AutoML image processing and TorchSharp features should remain unchanged.

## Compatibility

Some breaks are inherent in removing TensorFlow:

- Existing TensorFlow-backed Vision model archives require retraining. Reject them with a clear diagnostic rather than attempting to read them as the new format.
- TensorFlow-specific scoring/model APIs and the public `StringTensorFactory` helper are removed.
- SciSharp native-runtime packages are replaced by the appropriate ONNX Runtime prerequisites.
- TensorFlow-specific workspace and checkpoint formats change.

Handle legacy feature caches explicitly. Invalidate incompatible or unversioned caches rather than silently mixing features from different implementations.

Under this proposal, the classification head runs on CPU. The backbone may use a supported ONNX Runtime CPU or GPU provider. Document device selection and verify the performance implications rather than assuming parity with TensorFlow GPU execution.

Bitwise-identical training results are not required, but acceptable numerical, quality and performance differences must be established.

Issues.Title: Remove AwesomeAssertions and standardise on xUnit assertions
Issues.Body:
Remove the AwesomeAssertions dependency and migrate its remaining usages to xUnit assertions or existing repository assertion helpers.

AwesomeAssertions is referenced by four test projects, all of which use it. There are 261 `.Should()` call sites across 19 files, compared with roughly 7,700 `Assert.*` calls.

| Test project | Assertion call sites |
|---|---:|
| Microsoft.ML.SearchSpace.Tests | 144 |
| Microsoft.ML.AutoML.Tests | 109 |
| Microsoft.ML.Tests | 6 |
| Microsoft.ML.Fairlearn.Tests | 2 |

Most usages are straightforward assertions: 179 calls use `Be`, `BeTrue`, or `BeFalse`. The 21 `BeEquivalentTo` calls compare string collections or an empty numeric array rather than complex object graphs. There are no assertion scopes or custom fluent assertion infrastructure.

Standardising on xUnit would remove a redundant test dependency and reduce inconsistency across the test suite.

## Proposed changes

- Replace fluent assertions with xUnit assertions or existing repository helpers.
- Remove all 20 `FluentAssertions` imports, including the already-unused import in `OneDalEstimators.cs`.
- Remove the four `AwesomeAssertions` package references.
- Remove its central package entry from `Directory.Packages.props` and version property from `eng/Versions.props`.
- Update `.github/copilot-instructions.md` so it no longer recommends AwesomeAssertions. The current test-generation guidance does not recommend it and needs no removal. Leave historical release notes unchanged.

Issues.Title: Preserve LightGBM validation groups after dataset loading
Issues.Body:
Fixes #7759

## Summary

Preserve validation query boundaries when training a LightGBM ranker through ML.NET's `Fit(trainData, validationData)`.

## Root cause

LightGBM's `LGBM_DatasetCreateByReference` initializes the validation dataset's `query_` vector with zeros because the training dataset contains query information.

ML.NET supplies group sizes through LightGBM's `LGBM_DatasetSetField("group")`, but does not populate LightGBM's per-row `query_` vector. When ML.NET pushes the last validation rows through LightGBM's `LGBM_DatasetPushRows`, LightGBM's `FinishLoad()` rebuilds the query boundaries from the zero-filled `query_` vector and merges all validation rows into one query.

The training dataset does not have this issue because ML.NET creates it through LightGBM's `LGBM_DatasetCreateFromSampledColumn`, which leaves `query_` empty. LightGBM's `FinishLoad()` therefore does not rebuild its query boundaries.

## Fix

Apply the validation groups after ML.NET's `LoadDataset` completes. LightGBM's `LGBM_DatasetSetField("group")` then updates the query count, query boundaries, query weights, and CUDA metadata before the validation dataset is added to the booster.

## Tests

Added a regression test that verifies a ranking model can be trained with many validation groups.

## Additional information

LightGBM supports ranking metadata in two forms:

- Group sizes through `LGBM_DatasetSetField("group")`.
- Per-row query IDs through the streaming `LGBM_DatasetPushRowsWithMetadata` API.

ML.NET currently uses LightGBM's non-streaming `LGBM_DatasetPushRows` path, where query IDs cannot be supplied with each row. Switching to per-row query IDs would require moving ML.NET's dataset loader to the streaming API and extending its native wrappers and batch metadata handling.

LightGBM ranking only requires query boundaries, not the original query ID values, so group sizes remain a valid representation. Applying them after loading is therefore the smallest targeted fix.

Issues.Title: feat(DataFrame): Support CanShuffle and parallel cursor sets in IDataView
Issues.Body:
## Description

DataFrame's IDataView implementation hardcodes `CanShuffle => false` and `GetRowCursorSet` just returns a single cursor, even though DataFrame's columnar storage gives O(1) random row access. That means any ML.NET pipeline consuming a DataFrame as training data (via `DataFrameMLContextExtensions` or similar) can't shuffle rows or get parallel cursors, so you lose a basic trainer-level optimization that other IDataView sources support.

Changes:
- `CanShuffle` returns `true`.
- `GetRowCursor` uses a Fisher-Yates shuffle over a row-index permutation array when `rand != null`, leaving the unshuffled path untouched.
- `GetRowCursorSet` partitions `[0, Rows.Count)` into `n` roughly equal ranges and hands each cursor its own `Random` instance derived from the caller's seed, so cursors are safe to consume on separate threads.

## Related Issue

Fixes #6144

## Testing

Added `TestIDataView_CanShuffleAndShuffledCursor` and `TestIDataView_ParallelCursorSet` in `DataFrameIDataViewTests.cs`. Ran the full `Microsoft.Data.Analysis.Tests` suite locally: 490 passed, 0 failed.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "feat(DataFrame): Support CanShuffle and parallel cursor sets in IDataView" (#7764)

Issues.Title: Fix Apply<TResult> buffer boundary corruption when sizeof(T) != sizeof(TResult) (fixes #7122)
Issues.Body:
Fixes #7122.

### Description
When calling `Apply<TResult>` on a `PrimitiveDataFrameColumn` where `sizeof(T)` differs from `sizeof(TResult)` (for example, mapping `int` to `byte` or `float` to `double`), the container indexing logic incorrectly calculated the target buffer offset, leading to `IndexOutOfRangeException` or out-of-bounds memory writes.

This PR fixes the target buffer byte offset calculation in `PrimitiveColumnContainer.cs` so that elements are written into their correct slot regardless of type size differences.

Issues.Title: Respect null bitmaps in primitive column comparisons
Issues.Body:
Checks the null bitmap when comparing values in primitive columns.

## Description

Comparisons between primitive columns only evaluated the data buffers, so null values were compared as whatever the buffer held underneath (usually zero). The container now corrects the results using the validity bitmaps: two nulls are equal, and a null is only "not equal" to a value. Whole bitmap bytes with no nulls are skipped, and columns without nulls take no extra work. The same applies when comparing a column against a scalar.

##  Validation

- I've added a generator which creates tests for every combination of inputs across all primitive data types; might be overkill, there is a total of 860 new tests (861 including the line below this).
- There is also an `[X64Fact]` decorated test to ensure that the null checking works across buffers.

Fixes #6820
